learningObjectives: Define API Module Attributes for message elements.
Distinguish request and response defaults for Add and Add and buffer.
Update API Modules separately from attribute mappings.
Validate changed attributes before relying on test execution.

elements.text: Export generates API Modules used by TestSteps. Request steps supply values; response steps expose received data for assertions or reuse. Independent guidance: inspect references rather than assuming every exported artifact becomes unrelated.

Current documentation calls these Module Attributes. They expose business-relevant message elements, including payload, headers, parameters, authentication, attachments, method/endpoint/resource, status code and response time. Do not confuse this API mechanism with Reusable TestStepBlock Business Parameters.
Independent guidance: use a descriptive name and confirm the selected element before configuring a TestStep. A bare closing brace is not a reliable specification of an intended business element.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Defaults depend on direction and creation method

elements.text: Add uses Insert for request attributes and Verify for response attributes. Add and buffer on a request uses Insert with a DefaultValue buffer reference such as {B[name]}; on a response it uses Buffer with the element name as DefaultValue. It is incorrect to say the request workflow is unavailable.

Insert supplies a message value; whether that creates a server object depends on the operation contract. Independently inspect Value and ActionMode before execution and ensure a referenced buffer exists.
To refresh a Module from API Scan: select it in Commander, use API Scan > Open selected Modules, modify messages and click Update. An attribute for a changed element also needs its mapping updated.

For a ModuleAttribute mapping: select the attribute, highlight the new or changed payload element and use API Testing > Update. Check the resulting XPath; a body attribute update changes DefaultValue. Module edits are automatically applied to corresponding messages, so a blanket no-auto-update rule is wrong.

Select attributes, a Module, a containing folder, ComponentFolder or project root; run API Testing > Module Attribute > Validate. The dialog identifies invalid attributes and allows navigation to them. Validation is not proof of server behavior or all business assertions.

Independent guidance: inspect renamed elements and affected TestSteps, then execute targeted tests. A rename can leave a stale XPath; failure is a risk to investigate rather than a guaranteed outcome for every edit. This recap is independent, not a verified transcription of Academy slides.

Use a disposable request and response: insert input, verify an expected output, capture a returned identifier and reuse it in a later request. Change one payload element, update the mapping, validate and execute. Academy exercises and videos were not accessed.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing parameter mechanisms
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Equating API attributes with reusable-block parameters.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the ModuleAttribute and its message mapping.

examPitfalls.title: Ignoring response metadata
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define status/time checks when required alongside business assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Guessing a mapping from punctuation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a brace as proof of the intended element.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the selected element and resulting XPath.

examPitfalls.title: Misunderstanding request buffering
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Add and buffer cannot apply to requests.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A request uses Insert with a buffer reference; ensure the buffer is available.

examPitfalls.title: Combining different update workflows
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Scan Update repairs every attribute mapping.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Update changed attribute mappings separately and validate.

examPitfalls.title: Mistaking validation for a passing test
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming valid mappings prove correct server behavior.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Execute assertions against independently defined expected outcomes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Are API Module Attributes the same mechanism as Reusable TestStepBlock Business Parameters?

options.text: No; API attributes steer message elements.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect each mechanism in its own context.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API attributes are message mappings, not reusable-block argument definitions.

optionExplanations.C: Direction does not make them identical.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a TestCase check an expected HTTP status?

options.text: Define a status-code ModuleAttribute and verify the expected value.
Only body fields can be checked.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Status assertions can complement body assertions.

optionExplanations.B: This exposes the value for the assertion.
optionExplanations.C: Attributes are not limited to body fields.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A payload element changed. How do you retarget an existing ModuleAttribute?

options.text: Select the attribute, highlight the new element and use API Testing Update; inspect XPath.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Retargeting requires selecting the intended element.

optionExplanations.A: Punctuation alone does not specify the target.
optionExplanations.B: This updates the mapping to the selected element.
optionExplanations.D: Restarting is not this mapping-update workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does Add and buffer default to for a request ModuleAttribute?

options.text: Insert with a DefaultValue buffer reference.
Converts the request into a response.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The request consumes a buffer reference rather than capturing a returned value.

optionExplanations.B: This is the documented request behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Creation does not reverse message direction.
optionExplanations.D: It does not delete the selected element.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A payload field is renamed but an attribute still has its old XPath. What is the appropriate next step?

options.text: Inspect and update the mapping, validate it and test affected behavior.
Wait for a restart to repair it.

practiceQuiz.rationale: A rename may invalidate the selector; inspect rather than predict universal failure.

optionExplanations.B: This addresses the mapping and behavior risk.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming does not imply automatic deletion.
optionExplanations.D: Restarting is not a mapping repair.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After modifying messages opened from an existing Module in API Scan, how do you refresh that Module?

options.text: Assume every Scan edit instantly syncs.
Click Update; also update attributes for changed elements.

practiceQuiz.hint: Module refresh and mapping refresh are distinct.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Scan workflow explicitly updates the corresponding Module.

optionExplanations.A: Scan editing alone is not the documented refresh.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does API Scan Update do for a Module opened via Open selected Modules?

options.text: Updates the corresponding Commander API Module.

practiceQuiz.hint: The operation targets the opened Module.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Inspect updated content in Technical View.

optionExplanations.A: It does not require discarding all Modules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An attribute is created with Add on a request. What is its default ActionMode?
practiceQuiz.hint: The request supplies an input value.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Insert steers the request value; server-side effects depend on the API contract.

optionExplanations.A: Verify is the response Add default.
optionExplanations.C: Buffer is not this Add default.
optionExplanations.D: WaitOn is not this documented default.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An attribute is created with Add on a response. What is its default ActionMode?
practiceQuiz.hint: The response supplies an actual value to compare.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Verify compares the response with the configured expectation; inspect the applicable comparison settings.

optionExplanations.A: Insert is the request Add default.
optionExplanations.B: Verify is the response Add default.
optionExplanations.C: Add and buffer is a different workflow.
optionExplanations.D: WaitOn is not this documented default.

quickRecap.value: Named mappings to message elements, distinct from reusable-block parameters.
Request: Insert with buffer reference. Response: Buffer.
Scan refreshes Modules; changed element mappings need attribute Update.
Validate mappings, then execute business assertions.
